Article Title: SC ends decades-old power tussle, Himachal to get 11,973 MU from Punjab, Haryana
Article Text:
The BBMB has been providing Himachal Pradesh with its 7.19 per cent share of electricity from these projects since November 1, 2011. However, Punjab and Haryana had not cleared the outstanding dues for the earlier period, amounting to 13,066 MU.

What was the 2011 Supreme Court verdict?

How did the dispute reach the Supreme Court?

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday settled a decades-old inter-state dispute over unpaid electricity dues from Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB) projects, directing Punjab and Haryana to provide Himachal Pradesh with 11,973 million units (MU) of electricity over 20 years. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, along with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, accepted the Centre's proposal to clear the outstanding dues through an energy-based settlement instead of a cash payment.The settlement follows a 2011 Supreme Court verdict that recognised Himachal Pradesh's entitlement to a 7.19 per cent share in the electricity generated by the Bhakra Nangal and Beas hydroelectric projects. The dues date back to 1966, but Punjab and Haryana had not cleared the state's outstanding share for the period before November 2011.Under the arrangement approved by the top court, Punjab and Haryana will provide the electricity over 20 years. The settlement also factors in an adjustment of around Rs 420 crore towards Himachal Pradesh's share of the historical capital costs incurred in building the dams. As a result, the hill state will not have to make any separate payment to Punjab or Haryana.The Centre had earlier proposed that the 13,066 MU in outstanding electricity dues be paid over 15 years, at the rate of 871 MU annually during the lean seasons between October and March. However, the states could not agree on the proposed timeline.Punjab initially opposed the 15-year arrangement and later sought to extend the payment period to 30 years. Himachal Pradesh, on the other hand, wanted the dues cleared within 10 years. The Supreme Court's decision to settle the matter over 20 years brings an end to the prolonged disagreement over the payment schedule.The original electricity arrears were calculated at 13,066 MU by the Central Electricity Authority (CEA). The Centre's proposal had also factored in Himachal Pradesh's liability towards the capital costs of the Bhakra Nangal and Beas projects.According to a report by PTI, the proposal says that Himachal Pradesh's liability was assessed at Rs 420.7 crore, comprising Rs 249.2 crore payable to Punjab and Rs 171.5 crore to Haryana. This represented the state's 7.19 per cent share of the composite of Punjab's outstanding loan-servicing costs for the projects since 1966-67.The Centre had suggested setting off this liability against a portion of the electricity arrears. At the proposed rate of Rs 3.85 per unit, around 1,093 MU would have been adjusted against the capital cost liability.The proposal also provided for the distribution of electricity arrears between Punjab and Haryana in the inter-state ratio of 58:42 for the Bhakra Nangal project and 60:40 for the Beas projects. However, since the states could not reach a consensus on the applicable electricity rate, the Centre recommended settling the dues in energy terms.The Supreme Court's 2011 decision fixed Himachal Pradesh's share in the BBMB projects at 7.19 per cent. Punjab's share was set at 51.80 per cent, while Haryana was allocated 37.51 per cent. Rajasthan's share largely remained unchanged, and Chandigarh's share was fixed at 3.50 per cent.The verdict also specified when Himachal Pradesh's entitlement would take effect for the three projects. The state was entitled to a share in the Bhakra project from November 1, 1966, the Dehar project from November 1977 and the Pong Dam project from January 1978.The BBMB has been providing Himachal Pradesh with its 7.19 per cent share of electricity from these projects since November 1, 2011, PTI reported, citing sources. However, Punjab and Haryana had not cleared the outstanding dues for the earlier period, amounting to 13,066 MU.The dispute dates back to the reorganisation of Punjab under the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966. Himachal Pradesh maintained that, as a successor state, it was entitled to a 7.19 per cent share in the BBMB projects and their electricity generation.After efforts to resolve the disagreement between the neighbouring states failed, Himachal Pradesh approached the Supreme Court in 1996 through an original suit. It sought recognition of its entitlement to a share in the projects and the payment of the corresponding arrears.The Centre subsequently attempted to settle the matter outside court. However, with no agreement emerging between the states, the Supreme Court passed a decree on September 27, 2011, upholding Himachal Pradesh's 7.19 per cent entitlement.The latest order accepting the Centre's energy-based settlement provides a mechanism to clear the accumulated dues and closes a dispute that has remained unresolved for decades.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Monday settled a decades-old dispute over unpaid electricity dues from Bhakra Beas Management Board projects. Punjab and Haryana will provide Himachal Pradesh with 11,973 million units (MU) of electricity over 20 years. The dispute dates back to the reorganisation of Punjab under the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966.

Article Title: OBC creamy layer row: SC protects past jobs, promotions but leaves pending cases open
Article Text:
The government has maintained that it is not challenging or seeking a review of the March 11 judgment.

Centre flags concerns over past recruitments

Dispute over salary-based creamy layer criteria

Centre seeks time to frame uniform mechanism

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday clarified that its March 11 ruling on determining the creamy layer status of Other Backward Class (OBC) candidates would not reopen completed appointments, promotions or seniority positions.The top court said cases that are still pending would be examined individually by the courts, based on their merits and the candidates' eligibility.A bench of Justice Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha and Justice R Mahadevan delivered the ruling while hearing an application filed by the Centre seeking clarity on how the March 11 judgment should be implemented. The Court also extended the deadline for compliance with its earlier directions by eight weeks.The clarification comes after the Centre raised concerns that applying the March 11 ruling retrospectively could unsettle years of government recruitments, service allocations and admissions to educational institutions.In its application, the government argued that applying the revised interpretation to past cases could affect appointments and admissions made under the rules and eligibility criteria in force at the time.It warned that this could create uncertainty over OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression.“Retrospective or belated application of a changed eligibility criterion may unsettle appointments and admissions made under the rules and certificates prevailing at the relevant time and may create uncertainty regarding OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression. It may also affect admissions to Central and State educational institutions, universities and professional institutions. The Applicant therefore respectfully submits that the temporal operation of the Judgment requires clarification so as to avoid unsettling completed selections, appointments and admissions and the consequential rights arising therefrom”, the plea stated as per LiveLaw.The Centre said more than 5.69 lakh reserved vacancies, including 3.70 lakh OBC vacancies, were filled in Central government ministries, departments and their subordinate offices between 2016 and 2025.These recruitments were conducted under the August 8, 1993 Office Memorandum and subsequent government instructions.It argued that retrospective implementation could also necessitate a review of service allocations made through Civil Services Examinations since 2012. This could potentially lead to changes in the services and cadres allotted to officers already in government service, affecting their seniority and promotion prospects.The government also flagged possible complications in recruitment examinations conducted by the Railways, banks, Department of Posts and paramilitary organisations. It said similar disputes could arise in 18 States and Union Territories that follow the 1993 guidelines.The Centre further pointed out that candidates who become eligible for technical services several years after an examination might no longer meet the prescribed physical and medical standards. It also warned that reopening admissions granted to lakhs of students in universities and professional institutions could create difficulties, particularly where there are no provisions for additional seats.The clarification application stems from the Supreme Court's March 11 judgment on how the creamy layer among OBC candidates should be identified.The Court had ruled that a parent's salary alone cannot be used to determine whether an OBC candidate belongs to the creamy layer. The nature and category of the post held by the parents must also be taken into account.The dispute centred on two government instructions, the Office Memorandum issued on August 8, 1993, and a subsequent clarification dated October 14, 2004.The 1993 memorandum laid down the criteria for identifying the OBC creamy layer. It did not make a parent's salary the sole basis for exclusion from reservation benefits. Under the applicable Income/Wealth Test, salary and agricultural income are excluded from the income calculation, while the status and category of the parent's post remain relevant under the prescribed criteria.The 2004 clarification dealt with employees working in organisations such as public sector undertakings (PSUs), banks, universities and private companies, where the equivalence of their posts with government positions had not been established. It provided for consideration of parents' salary income in such cases.The Supreme Court held that the 2004 clarification could not introduce a new condition that was not part of the original 1993 policy. It also observed that treating children of PSU and private-sector employees differently from those of similarly placed government employees could amount to hostile discrimination and violate Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution, which guarantee equality before the law and equal opportunity in public employment.The government has maintained that it is not challenging or seeking a review of the March 11 judgment. Instead, it wants clarity on when the ruling should apply and how its directions should be implemented.The Centre has sought two years to consult stakeholders, establish equivalence between posts in non-government organisations and government positions, and develop a uniform mechanism for determining creamy-layer status in cases where such equivalence has not been established.It has also asked the SC not to disturb completed selections, appointments, service and cadre allocations, seniority positions and admissions made under the eligibility rules applicable at the time. The government has separately sought clarity on candidates who were already participating in examinations or recruitment processes when the March 11 judgment was delivered.In a separate interim application, the Centre sought permission to proceed with service allocation for 958 candidates recommended by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in the Civil Services Examination 2025, using the existing 1993 framework while the clarification application remained pending.The government argued that any further delay would push back the candidates' Foundation Course, training and induction schedules. It said the resulting disruption could not be reversed even if the Court eventually accepted its position.
Article Summary: The top court said cases that are still pending would be examined individually by the courts, based on their merits and the candidates' eligibility. The Court also extended the deadline for compliance with its earlier directions by eight weeks. The Centre raised concerns that applying the March 11 ruling retrospectively could unsettle years of government recruitments.

Article Title: 'Will be dealt with iron hand': SC issues contempt notice to Kerala Congress over controversial CJI post
Article Text:
SC sends notice to Kerala Congress over CJI post

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has issued a contempt notice to office-bearers of the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) over a social media post targeting Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, observing that freedom of expression cannot be used as a shield to interfere with the administration of justice.The apex court said, "Judgments are always open to criticism but freedom of expression can't be a shield for interference with administration of justice.""Any attempt to undermine authority of court needs to be dealt with iron hand," it further said, as cited by PTI.Reiterating the supremacy of the Constitution, the court added, "Constitution is supreme, no individual or political organisation stands above it."The Supreme Court has registered a petition based on a complaint seeking contempt proceedings against the KPCC over the social media post. According to the apex court's website, a complaint addressed to the CJI by advocate Vineet Jindal on October 13 was registered as a writ petition on October 30.The complaint also sought directions to authorities to ascertain whether a political demonstration and slogan-shouting held on the Supreme Court premises on the evening of October 12, 2026, involving Rahul Gandhi and other political leaders, took place without authorisation or caused any obstruction to the movement of advocates, litigants, judicial officers or court staff.A post targeting the CJI from the official Congress Kerala account on X went viral on October 12, drawing sharp criticism on social media, before being deleted. The party subsequently removed the person responsible for publishing it.In a statement, KPCC president Sunny Joseph said the person responsible for posting the controversial message on the party's official X account had been removed from the charge. He clarified that the post was made without the knowledge, consent or consultation of the KPCC leadership.Joseph also said the Congress party had no disagreement with regard to the impartiality of the judiciary.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court has issued a contempt notice to office-bearers of the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) over a social media post targeting Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant. A post targeting the CJI from the official Congress Kerala account on X went viral on October 12, drawing sharp criticism on social media, before being deleted.

Article Title: 2013 Tehelka rape case: SC refuses to suspend Tarun Tejpal's 10-year jail term
Article Text:
Tejpal had approached the Supreme Court challenging the Bombay high court's August 6 judgment

What Tejpal argued

Goa government opposes relief

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday refused to suspend the 10-year prison sentence of former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal , convicted of raping a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator in Goa in November 2013.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale dismissed Tejpal's application after considering the evidence, including his emails and messages. The bench was of the view that no case had been made out for suspending his sentence, according to Live Law.Tejpal had approached the Supreme Court challenging the Bombay high court's August 6 judgment, which overturned his acquittal by a trial court in 2021 and convicted him in the case.Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Tejpal, questioned the victim's account of the incident, particularly her claim that the elevator doors did not open during the alleged assault.Sibal argued that technical evidence showed the elevator doors opened twice during the two minutes and nine seconds in which the alleged incident took place. He said the hotel manager and Mitsubishi staff had testified that the lift doors opened automatically at every floor and could not be kept shut by pressing the buttons.He also questioned the investigation, alleging that the investigating officer failed to seize CCTV footage that could have established whether the elevator doors had opened.Tejpal's lawyers further argued that the victim had given six versions of the incident before the FIR was registered on November 22, 2013, and that none of them mentioned rape or oral penetration. They also stressed that Tejpal had remained on bail during the trial and had not misused his liberty.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Goa government, opposed the plea and referred to messages and an apology email sent by Tejpal to the victim after the incident.Sibal countered that the apology had been drafted by then Tehelka editor Shoma Chaudhary and claimed it referred to a conversation between Tejpal and the woman, not an admission of rape.The case relates to allegations that Tejpal sexually assaulted a junior colleague inside an elevator at a luxury hotel during a Tehelka event in Goa in November 2013.A Goa trial court acquitted him in 2021. However, the Bombay High Court's Goa bench overturned the acquittal on August 6, 2026, convicted him of rape and other offences, and sentenced him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court refused to suspend the 10-year prison sentence of former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal. He was convicted of raping a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator in Goa in November 2013. A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale dismissed his application after considering the evidence.

Article Title: IMA asks CBFC to deny certification to Sunny Deol-starrer, flags glorification of violence against doctors
Article Text:
The association said the objectionable content is the film's core theme and cannot be removed by mere excisions.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has urged the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) to refuse a certificate for the upcoming Hindi film Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak, starring Sunny Deol and Ravi Kishan, alleging that its teaser glorifies violence against doctors and hospital staff at a time when attacks on healthcare workers are a growing concern.In a detailed representation to the CBFC chairperson, the IMA said the film portrays a father who loses his daughter and takes revenge on those he holds responsible, with scenes showing him assaulting doctors and hospital staff inside a hospital. The association objected to dialogues in the teaser that accuse doctors of demanding excessive payments, ordering unnecessary tests and writing commission slips instead of prescriptions.The IMA argued that the film presents violence as a justified response to grievances against hospitals and could encourage attacks on medical professionals. It cited provisions of the Cinematograph Act, 1952, arguing that the content could incite offences, threaten public order and defame registered medical practitioners as a group.The representation comes against the backdrop of repeated attacks on healthcare workers.Citing a survey of 1,566 healthcare workers by experts from VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital and AIIMS, reported in May 2026, the IMA said 58.2 per cent felt unsafe at their workplace, and 78.4 per cent had faced threats while on duty. It also referred to an earlier IMA study that found more than 75 per cent of doctors had faced workplace violence.The association cited several incidents, including the killing of 22-year-old intern Dr Vandana Das in Kerala in May 2023, the assault on a doctor at Thamarassery in October 2025 and attacks on resident doctors in Aligarh in May 2026. It also referred to recent assaults in Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Telangana.The IMA said violence against doctors disrupts medical services and creates fear among healthcare workers, affecting patients as well. Citing Supreme Court observations on the issue, it has urged the CBFC to deny certification to the film and its promotional material if they depict violence against healthcare workers or portray doctors as corrupt. Alternatively, it has sought referral to a Revising Committee, a screening for IMA representatives and a medical expert, and removal of scenes that glorify or justify such violence. The association has also sought a hearing before the Board decides, citing the film’s scheduled nationwide release on November 20.
Article Summary: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has urged the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) to refuse a certificate for the upcoming Hindi film Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak. The association said the film portrays a father who loses his daughter and takes revenge on those he holds responsible, with scenes showing him assaulting doctors and hospital staff inside a hospital.

NEW DELHI: Referring to the contradictory orders given by Supreme Court in the matter of bail to the accused on the ground of delay in trial and long incarceration for UAPA offences, which have been referred to a larger bench for authoritative pronouncement, former student activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have moved SC for bail in 2020 Delhi riots cases.The accused submitted that two co-accused, including Tasleem Ahmed, were granted bail by SC on the grou-nd that determination of the issues by the larger bench would take time, and they could not be made to suffer continued incarceration.Seeking parity with the co-accused, Sharjeel Imam, who has already spent six years and nine months in custody, said in his petition, filed through advocate Fauzia Shakil, that two co-accused in the same FIR were released on interim bail by the court on May 22 under a principle which applies to him in greater degree.The accused moved SC after their plea for bail was rejected by the trial court and Delhi High Court on the ground that the apex court had purportedly set a deadline of Jan 5, 2027, for them to file a bail petition.The petition asked "whether the principle recognised by this Court in Tasleem Ahmed v. State order dated 22.05.2026, that an accused cannot be made to suffer continued incarceration merely because an important question of law has arisen for authoritative settlement, can be withheld from the petitioner alone by reference to the role attributed to him, when the question referred to concerns the correctness of the very judgment which declined his bail and relief in Tasleem Ahmed case was granted without any examination of role?"It further argued, "Whether liberty reserved by this Court in a judgment declining bail, to renew the prayer for bail at a defined point, operates as a bar upon the statutory jurisdiction of the Special Court and of the High Court to consider an application for bail founded on supervening circumstances be-fore that point, when the same paragraph of the judgment holds that pre-trial detention cannot be permitted to continue without regard to the progress of the trial and that Article 21 operates as a continuing check against continued incarceration without substantial progress of the trial?"
Article Summary: Former student activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have moved SC for bail in 2020 Delhi riots cases. The accused submitted that two co-accused, including Tasleem Ahmed, were granted bail by SC on the grou-nd that determination of the issues by the larger bench would take time.

Article Title: 'No impact on India-US ties': Tharoor says Trump retains power on tariffs, Iran war
Article Text:
He also highlighted the gains made by candidates from minority communities and people of Indian origin

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Friday said the results of the US midterm elections would have little impact on India-US relations, asserting that President Donald Trump retains considerable powers to pursue his foreign policy agenda despite the ruling party's electoral setback.Speaking in Thiruvananthapuram, Tharoor said the US election results would not change Washington's approach towards key issues such as tariffs, sanctions on countries buying Russian oil, the Iran war or the Ukraine conflict."Whether it comes to tariffs, whether it comes to sanctions for buying Russian oil, whether it comes to the Iran war itself, whether it comes to any initiative he takes on the Ukraine war. All of this, he's completely unaffected by the election result," Tharoor said.He explained that while Congress has significant powers over budgetary matters and can restrict or approve government spending, the President enjoys considerable discretion in foreign policy and international affairs.Tharoor said that even when it comes to military action, the President can proceed without seeking approval for an initial period of up to 60 days. However, Congress can exercise its financial powers to restrict expenditure, particularly in the case of an expensive military campaign."Those in India who are expecting this to have some impact on our relationship with the US, I think, are completely mistaken," he said.Commenting on the election outcome, Tharoor described it as an extraordinary setback for the ruling party, pointing out that midterm elections traditionally serve as a course correction for the party in power.He also highlighted the gains made by candidates from minority communities and people of Indian origin, including the election of a mayor of Indian origin in Los Angeles.Tharoor said the results reflected the vibrancy of American democracy but maintained that the outcome would not significantly alter Trump's ability to take decisions on international affairs.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said the results of the US midterm elections would have little impact on India-US relations. He said President Donald Trump retains considerable powers to pursue his foreign policy agenda despite the ruling party's electoral setback. He also highlighted the gains made by candidates from minority communities and people of Indian origin.

NEW DELHI: Indian Youth Congress has suspended over 300 office-bearers from the organisation for not showing up for the 'Chalo Delhi' rally of INDIA bloc Sunday - a significant step to drive home the message that the outfit is serious about mass mobilisation in future.IYC sources said organisational office-bearers from assembly to the central level were directed to attend the rally with Rahul Gandhi as the face. NEW DELHI: NCP leader Praful Patel on Thursday visited Nationalist Congress Party (SP) chief Sharad Pawar at Mumbai’s Breach Candy Hospital and enquired about his health. Patel said the veteran politician was stable and expected to return home in a day or two after completing his medical check-ups.The visit by Patel has triggered political speculation as he is among the NCP leaders reportedly "unhappy" with party boss Sunetra Pawar’s leadership. The meeting comes amid signs of internal discord within the party, adding a political dimension to Patel’s hospital visit.Sharad Pawar was admitted to Breach Candy Hospital on Wednesday night with a respiratory and chest infection, after being discharged from Pune’s Ruby Hall Clinic. Dr Pratit Samdani, a doctor at the hospital, said on Thursday that Pawar was stable and undergoing treatment."Sharad Pawar was admitted yesterday at Breach Candy Hospital for a respiratory and chest infection. He is stable and under treatment. He was admitted last night; he had a cough and an infection, something like bronchitis trouble. His treatment is ongoing, and he is currently stable," Dr Samdani told reporters.After meeting Pawar, Patel said the hospital admission was part of his routine medical check-ups and that his health was good. He also dismissed speculation that their meeting involved political discussions, saying he continued to meet Pawar and his daughter, Supriya Sule, because of their family ties.Also read: Rest, Supriya and I’ll look after country, PM Narendra Modi said to have told Sharad Pawar In a post on X, Patel said, "I visited the Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai to pay a courtesy call on the esteemed Shri Sharad Pawar Saheb and inquired about his health."Providing an update on Pawar's condition, Patel said, "Sharad Pawar due to fatigue two days ago, was taken to Ruby Hall Clinic in Pune for a checkup. After that, he came to Mumbai, and here his health is fine. Naturally, a checkup happens once or twice a year, for a complete checkup, so in that context only he is admitted here at Breach Candy. His health is good. I am also happy that I came here, but everything is fine, and sahab was also in good spirits. He was asking about what is happening in politics in the country and state, as that is his interest. We had a good conversation, and I am happy that in a day or two all his checkups will be completed, so he will return home soon so he can rest."Patel also commented on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's conversation with Pawar, describing their relationship as long-standing and cordial. He said Modi's call to enquire about Pawar's health was natural given their association over the years.“Sharad Pawar and Narendra Modi have had a very long-standing relationship. I have also known Modi ji for many years and personally know about the relationship between him and Pawar sahab... I have witnessed their very good, cordial and respectful relationship over the years, even when we were in the UPA government in Delhi, and Modi ji was the Chief Minister of Gujarat... NEW DELHI: The Union home ministry has relaxed passport and visa requirements for several categories of foreign nationals residing in India, including Pakistani citizens who entered prior to December 31, 2009 with the intention to permanently reside in India but could not renew their Pakistani passport due to non-possession of computerised nationality identity card issued by Pakistan government.Other categories of foreign nationals for whom passport and visa rules have been eased as part of the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) (Amendment) ORder, 2026, include citizens of Pakistan, Afghanistan and Pakistan belonging to their religious minorities; Sri Lankan Tamil refugees and Tibetans.The order also streamlines travel and identification protocols for the citizens of Nepal and Bhutan, allowing them to enter or exit India by producing any one of the documents specified in the visa manual; However, in case they are entering or exiting India from or to a place other than Nepal or Bhutan, they must in possession of a valid passport. Nepal and Bhutan citizens who have embarked at or transited through China Macau, Hong Kong or Pakistan, must be in possession of both a valid passport and valid visa.The requirement of a valid passport and visa would also not apply to a male member of the Muslim community, being originally an Indian citizen, who went to Pakistan after partition between August 15, 1947 and Dec 31, 1965 leaving behind family in India and returned to India on or before Dec 31, 2009, and settled in Keralam on a valid Pakistani passport but which has since expired or been lost.However, such a person should not have married or acquired immoveable property while in Pakistan; ,while going to Pakistan, left behind family members who are Indian citizens; shall not return to Pakistan; and should not have any adverse report from the police or security agencies.A citizen of India entering into India from Nepal or Bhutan or departing from India to Nepal or Bhutan by land or air shall produce before the immigration officer one of the documents specified in the visa manual to establish their identity, though this exemption would not be applicable if departing to or returning from countries other than Nepal or Bhutan through the Indo-Nepal or Indo-Bhutan border of by air. In all such cases, a valid passport will be required and the exit and entry into India shall be only through the designated immigration points.The provisions in the Act and rules with regard to requirement of valid passport or other valid travel document and valid visa for entry into, stay in and exit from India, shall also not apply for a member of naval, military or air forces of India, entering into or exiting from India on duty and members of the family of any such person when accompanying him on a government transport; registered Sri Lankan Tamil nationals who have taken shelter in India up to Jan 9, 2015; as well as the foreign crew of foreign military vessels coming for repairs in India who are granted military ship repair permits by the immigration officer, provided they hold their military identification documents.Exempted categories include a Tibetan who has entered India after 1959 but before May 30,, 2003 on an entry permit issued by the Embassy of India in Kathmandu; or who entered after May 30, 2003, on the special entry permit issued through the designated immigration post on the Indo-Nepal border and a certificate of registration was issued by the registration officer concerned.Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Christian, Jain and Parsi citizens of Pakistan who entered India before Dec 31, 2024, fearing religious persecution in their home country, without valid documents including passport or other travel documents; or with valid documents including passport that has since expired, would also get relief under the amended Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) order. However, such a person shall be required to obtain an appropriate category of visa after their entry into India, for continued stay.Also exempt now from requirement of a valid passport and visa are persons of Indian origin who subsequently acquired the citizenship of Malaysia or Singapore and returned to India on or before Dec 31, 2009 on a valid passport issued by either of those countries, which has since expired and is not being renewed by those countries because such person does not meet the conditions specified by those countries. Such persons must have documentary proof that they are a person of Indian origin.
Article Summary: The order also streamlines travel and identification protocols for the citizens of Nepal and Bhutan. Pakistani citizens who entered prior to December 31, 2009 could not renew their Pakistani passport due to non-possession of computerised nationality identity card. Other categories of foreign nationals for whom passport and visa rules have been eased include citizens of Pakistan, Afghanistan and Pakistan belonging to their religious minorities.

Article Title: ‘Speedy trial is a fundamental right’: SC says Constitution has primacy over special laws
Article Text:
Supreme Court of India

'

Speedy trial

is a fundamental right, can't tinker'

SC: Constitution should be guide to interpret law, not the other way round

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Should fundamental rights take precedence over special laws like NDPS and UAPA? Definitely. No, special laws should prevail. Depends on the individual case. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Constitution will prevail over all other laws and regulations, Supreme Court said on Thursday and made it clear that in case of any contradiction or conflict between constitutional provisions and special laws like NDPS, UAPA and PMLA, it is the former which will triumph.It reiterated that the right to speedy trial was a fundamental right and could not be violated under any law and could be the ground for bail.The bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and A S Chandurkar faulted the apex court's earlier order, which held that under special statutes such as NDPS Act, an accused's right under Article 21 (speedy trial) must be exercised within the confines of Section 37 of the Act (stringent bail conditions) and cannot be invoked solely on the ground of prolonged delay to override Section 37.The latest ruling comes amid sharp differences within the apex court over granting bail in PMLA, NDPS and UAPA cases on grounds of delay in trial, with the issue now before a larger bench.Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and A S Chandurkar also said fundamental rights cannot be tinkered with so lightly, not even under the special statutes.The bench said, "First and foremost, the rights conferred by Article 21 of the Constitution are not only constitutional rights.These are fundamental rights. Right to life and liberty as enshrined in Article 21 are at the core of our constitutional jurisprudence. These fundamental rights cannot be tinkered with so lightly, not even under the special statutes."Such observations run counter to numerous judgements of this court which reiterate the proposition that when there is a violation of Article 21 of the Constitution, the rigour of Section 37 of Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act or similar such provisions under special statutes would have to give way, the court said.The court's observation assumes significance as there are differences of opinion within Supreme Court on the issue of bail in offences under Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), NDPS and Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA) on grounds of delay in trial. Contradictory orders have been passed on whether the fundamental right to have a speedy trial would prevail over stringent bail conditions stipulated under special laws, with one bench saying the right to speedy trial cannot be the ground to grant bail in PMLA, UAPA offences while other benches took contradictory stands.The controversy now stands referred to a larger bench after two benches took swipes at each other in their judicial orders. "A statute, special or otherwise, cannot be a guide to interpret the Constitution; rather, it should be the other way round. To reiterate, a fundamental right must be interpreted in such a manner that it upholds and furthers the objective of such a fundamental right," the bench said, adding, "The court must interpret the Constitution in a manner which would enable citizens to enjoy the rights guaranteed by it in the fullest measure. "
Article Summary: Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and A S Chandurkar said fundamental rights cannot be tinkered with so lightly, not even under the special statutes. Ruling comes amid sharp differences within the apex court over granting bail in PMLA, NDPS and UAPA cases on grounds of delay in trial.

NEW DELHI: In a “Diwali gift” to travellers, Air India has once again made its flights between Delhi/Mumbai and New York (JFK and Newark EWR) nonstop since Wednesday, shaving close to four hours from the travel time of the one-stops these had become since the US-Iran war broke out this Feb 28. The airline's operations team, like that of other carriers, does constantly analyses enroute geopolitical situation and as soon as the risk rating for Iraq, Syria and Jordan reduced, it has started got a slightly shorter route available making the flights between Delhi and EWR; Delhi and JFK; Mumbai and EWR and Mumbai and JFK nonstop once again, skipping the Rome Fiumicino stop. Now the journeys become 15-16 hours, instead of the almost 20 hours they took with the Rome stop.The closure of Pakistan airspace since last April had made routes longer between Delhi and the west but the Iran airspace was open till Feb 28 when the US-Iran war broke out. Since then, the non-availability of Iran, Iraq and other enroute airspaces forced fuelling stops to be added. Now while Iran remains out of bounds, the Iraq airspace has become available and AI flight operations has seized the opportunity to make the New York flights nonstops again.While no one knows when and if Pakistan airspace will reopen for Indian carriers, AI is hoping that Iran airspace opens so that it can add more nonstops to the west. As of now in the current situation, its flights between Delhi/Mumbai and New York are likely to remain nonstop in Nov and Dec. From Jan, the winds become very strong and if the loads are high then fuelling stops may return for some time.“There is load penalty (restriction in number of passengers and/or cargo to carry more fuel for longer routes) since Pakistan airspace closed. So that remains. What has changed for now is that Iraq has become available again and made the flights nonstops again,” said pilots who operate this route.With the devastating economic impact of the US-Iran war on the midterms and Republicans facing a rout there, there is hope that the war will come to an end. If that happens, AI will add much more capacity to the west, including North America.

Article Title: 24-hour deadline starts with detention: SC
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday ruled that the constitutional mandate of producing an arrestee before a magistrate within 24 hours starts the moment one is detained for interrogation and not from the time when formal arrest is made by an investigating agency, since the liberty of a person is curtailed when one is detained.Noting that no artificial distinction should be created between detention and arrest, a bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar quashed the verdicts of high courts which had held that the 24-hour period starts only after formal arrest and not during antecedent detention necessitated by statutory procedure of seizure. Article 22(2) mandates that every person who is arrested and detained in custody has to be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours of such arrest."Article 22(2) does not sanction exclusion of the time taken for enquiry and investigation before the arresting authority could effect arrest of the detainee. This is beyond the mandate of Article 22(2) of the Constitution. Article 22(2) does not sanction creation of any buffer zone where the liberty of an individual is curtailed for investigating purposes but not formally shown as arrested. Creation or contemplation of such buffer zone is unconstitutional..." the bench said.As it is common practice for police to record formal arrest much later, sometimes even a day after detaining a person for interrogation, Supreme Court's order would serve as a check on the police and other investigating agencies. The court also noted that its order was meant to eliminate custodial violence, which unfortunately takes place during the time when a person is under detention and not shown as formally arrested, in the process delaying production before the magistrate.
Article Summary: Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar quashed verdicts of high courts. High courts had held that the 24-hour period starts only after formal arrest. The court also noted that its order was meant to eliminate custodial violence.

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission has reallocated work among its deputy election commissioners (DEC) and directors-general in view of the recent appointment of DEC Prakash Rajpurohit. DG (IT) Seema Khanna, who heads the division that manages the ECINet portal and application, will now put up all files regarding the IT/ICT and grievances divisions under her charge through senior DEC Pawan Kumar Sharma Sources in the commission said Khanna - whose name cropped up after Indian Express reported on Sept 23, 2026, that election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected to the alleged "centralisation" of ECINET, with access restricted for even authorised field officers - was earlier putting up these files through senior DEC Maneesh Garg, and before that through then DEC Sanjay Kumar.Though Garg had, while officiating as DEC (administration) during the leave period of DEC Bhanu Prakash Yeturu in July, issued a work allocation order that allowed Khanna to no longer route her files through then DEC Sanjay Kumar, this order was never implemented after the two election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected. This is recorded in the affidavit filed recently by EC in the Supreme Court."The work redistribution orders issued by the officer concerned were never implemented after the orders of the two commissioners, and the oversight of the IT division by the DEC was never actually withdrawn," EC said in the affidavit issued with approval of the full commission.Khanna, as a result, continued routing files through Sanjay Kumar, and after his stint with Election Commission ended, through Kumar's link officer Maneesh Garg.Under the work reallocation order dated Nov 4, Pawan Kumar Sharma will be the new deputy election commissioner in-charge of the IT/ICT as well as grievance/PGRS divisions, and Khanna would put up files of these divisions through him.Sandhu and Joshi had written separate letters to cabinet secretary T V Somanathan in July end, complaining about the working of senior Garg. In the near-identical letters, they said that Garg, soon after assuming charge as link officer of then DEC (administration) Yeturu, who was on leave, had issued an order regarding work allocation among senior DECs, DGs and equivalent officers, without discussing the revised allocation with the commission or the two election commissioners.This, Sandhu and Joshi said, was despite repeated oral instructions to all officers concerned against taking such actions without prior approval of the commission.The cabinet secretary had merely forwarded the election commissioners' letter to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, apart from sending an acknowledgement to the two commissioners. As per the file noting furnished by the cabinet secretariat in reply to an RTI application by Commodore Lokesh Batra (Retd), it was stated that any action against Garg "at this stage may be inappropriate" as the letters were not sent by the commission as a whole. "It may also be construed as interference in the functioning of the constitutional body," it was stated.
Article Summary: The Election Commission has reallocated work among its deputy election commissioners (DEC) and directors-general. NEW DELHI: Centre's move to consider a fresh review of the controversial UGC equity regulations are being seen as an olive branch to agitating upper caste groups, while giving BJP room to avoid a fresh caste controversy ahead of the assembly elections, particularly in Uttar Pradesh.The regulations, which extended specific protection against caste-based discrimination to OBCs alongside SCs and STs, had triggered protests among general category students who feared exclusion and possible misuse of the provisions.Centre told Supreme Court Thursday that it was contemplating setting up a committee to reconsider the regulations, ensuring that no section of students felt excluded or apprehensive. The move gives govt time to revisit the issue without committing itself to either withdrawing or retaining the rules.A complete rollback has been a key demand of upper caste organisations, whose protests also caused unease within BJP. Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh have been leading govt's outreach to agitating youth outfits. Both had met representatives of Kshatriya Karni Sena-led 'UGC Rollback Campaign' in Sept, after which a proposed mahapanchayat was postponed.The Jan notification had caused resentment among sections of general category students who felt the regulations portrayed upper castes as the principal perpetrators of caste discrimination. The absence of a specific provision against false complaints added to their concerns.At the heart of the controversy is the wording of the regulations. While one provision defines caste-based discrimination specifically as unfair treatment of SC, ST and OBC members, another prohibits discrimination against any student, including on caste grounds.General category students argue that this creates confusion over whether they would receive the same protection if they face caste-based discrimination.Supporters of the regulations argue that historically disadvantaged communities need specific safeguards against discrimination.For BJP, a complete withdrawal carries political risks. OBCs and Dalits form an important part of its social coalition, especially in Uttar Pradesh, where caste identities remain politically sensitive.
Article Summary: The regulations extended specific protection against caste-based discrimination to OBCs alongside SCs and STs. Centre told Supreme Court Thursday that it was contemplating setting up a committee to reconsider the regulations. The move gives govt time to revisit the issue without committing itself to either withdrawing or retaining the rules.

SRINAGAR: Kashmir has just one active local terrorist and recruitment in the valley completely stopped this year, while security forces were tracking a handful of foreign terrorists believed to be assisting him, J&K police IG Sujit Kumar said Thursday.Police identified the lone local terrorist as Mohammad Lateef Bhat, a resident of Khrewan Chader village in south Kashmir’s Kulgam district. A Rs 15 lakh reward was announced in Aug for information leading to his arrest. Bhat is accused of killing a head constable and two migrant workers in separate attacks in Anantnag and Kulgam in July. He is believed to have joined terrorist ranks last year.“No local has joined terrorist ranks this year. Local recruitment has completely dried up,” Kumar said. He added that the number of foreign terrorists could not be established as they kept moving between locations. “Giving their figure would be an exaggeration,” he said.Head constable Ashiq Hussain’s murder on July 22 was the first terrorist attack in Kashmir since the massacre of 25 tourists and a local pony operator in Pahalgam on April 22 last year.On restrictions imposed on civilian traffic during Army convoy movement since the Pahalgam attack, Kumar said security protocols reflected past terrorist strikes and continuing threat inputs. He said the matter was on the radar and would be discussed with other agencies. Article Title: 'Memory of the world': Rajatarangini, Mahabharata & Arthashastra get UN recognition
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Three major works of India's literary, historical and intellectual heritage, Kalhana's 'Rajatarangini', the 'Mahabharata' and Kautilya 's 'Arthashastra', have been added to Unesco's Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific.The decision was taken at the 11th session of the Memory of the World Committee for Asia and the Pacific (MOWCAP), held in Jakarta, Indonesia.The development was announced by Dr Sachchidanand Joshi, member secretary of the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA), which contributed to preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.In 2024, India had secured regional register recognition for three other literary works: The Ramcharitmanas, Panchatantra and Sahṛdayālokalocana.With the latest additions, India's total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six.Composed in the 12th century, Kalhana's 'Rajatarangini' provides a chronological account of Kashmir's rulers, political developments and the region's social and cultural life. Its approach to documenting history through evidence, traditions and critical inquiry gives it a distinct place in Indian historiography.The 'Mahabharata', one of the major epics of Indian civilisation, explores themes including Dharma, duty, justice, power and human relationships. Its philosophical reflections and enduring values have also made it part of South Asia's shared cultural memory.Kautilya's 'Arthashastra' deals with governance, statecraft, economic policy, diplomacy, administration and strategic affairs. The work reflects ancient India's political and administrative thinking and its understanding of the functioning of the state.The three inscriptions represent different aspects of India's intellectual traditions, spanning historical writing, philosophy and ethical thought, and governance.The announcement also comes amid efforts under the Gyan Bharatam Mission to preserve, promote and digitise India's manuscript heritage. The initiative aims to identify, conserve and digitise manuscripts across the country and make them accessible to future generations and the global community.
Article Summary: Kalhana's 'Rajatarangini', the 'Mahabharata' and Kautilya's 'Arthashastra' have been added to Unesco's Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the memory committee in Jakarta, Indonesia. The announcement comes amid efforts under the Gyan Bharatam Mission to preserve, promote and digitise India's manuscript heritage.

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Thursday said there is no change in the supervisory authority to which its director general of information technology Seema Khanna reports.The clarification came a day after the panel issued a fresh work allocation placing Khanna under the charge of deputy election commissioner Prakash Raj Purohit instead of senior deputy EC Manish Garg.A controversy had erupted after Garg issued an order on July 28 asking Khanna to report directly to the Election Commission, comprising Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Vivek Joshi and SS Sandhu.Garg had issued the order after deputy EC Sanjay Kumar, to whom Khanna had been reporting, was transferred to the Delhi government. The change effectively removed an intermediary layer of oversight, allowing Khanna to report directly to the Election Commission.ECs Sandhu and Joshi objected to the order and subsequently wrote separate letters to cabinet secretary TV Somanathan, raising concerns over the distribution of responsibilities.The order was then put in abeyance. The EC also told the Supreme Court that the July 28 work allocation order was never implemented.Asked whether Khanna had reported directly to the Commission between July 28 and November 4, without an added layer of a reporting boss in the form of a deputy EC, an election official on Thursday said: "Since the order was not implemented, Khanna was supervised by Garg after Sanjay Kumar moved out of the EC. Now, she will report to Raj Purohit, who joined as deputy EC a few days ago."Garg was the "link officer" for Kumar, which meant that Kumar's assigned tasks were transferred to Garg after he left the Election Commission.Khanna's role had come under scrutiny amid concerns over the functioning of the electoral roll software and the exercise of powers by Electoral Registration Officers (EROs).According to a report by The Indian Express, the two Election Commissioners were concerned that field-level officers, who are legally responsible for preparing electoral rolls, were unable to perform certain functions because the software did not permit them to do so.The permissions required to carry out these functions were reportedly controlled by the EC's IT division, headed by Khanna.The commissioners repeatedly raised concerns that powers legally vested in EROs were being increasingly centralised through the EC's IT system, potentially restricting the authority of officers responsible for preparing and revising electoral rolls.

Article Title: ‘Vote gone, rights gone’: Rahul alleges BJP conspiracy in schemes linked with voter ID instead of Aadhaar

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday launched a sharp attack on the Centre over Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh's announcement that voter ID cards would be used instead of Aadhaar to identify beneficiaries of social welfare programmes under the ministry of panchayati raj.Calling the move a "conspiracy", the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha alleged that linking welfare benefits to voter IDs could put people's access to government schemes at risk.In a post on X, Rahul claimed that the announcement was part of a wider attempt to remove names from electoral rolls through the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). He alleged that millions of names were being deleted under the exercise and that those most critical of the BJP were being targeted."Modi government minister's announcement - Benefits of schemes will now be determined not by Aadhaar, but by Voter ID. The conspiracy runs very deep—take your time to understand it. Under the guise of SIR, millions of names are being struck off voter lists—if not stopped, even more will be removed. Whose names are being targeted the most? Those who are furious with the BJP," Rahul said.He also accused the Election Commission of India (ECI) of colluding with the BJP, alleging that electoral rolls were no longer being maintained by an impartial body.Rahul named Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of being a "Modi government employee" and claiming that his alleged collusion with the BJP in "vote theft" had been exposed with evidence."The preparation is underway to craft such a list where the majority is always BJP's—and now that very list will decide whether you get scheme benefits or not. Anyone who decided yesterday that the BJP must go—will have their names cherry-picked and struck off. Name struck—vote gone. Vote gone—rights gone. And just like that, you'll become invisible citizens of a hijacked democracy—where the people don't elect the government, the government selects its people," he added.Rahul further warned that making voter ID mandatory for welfare benefits could eventually affect access to ration, pensions, MGNREGA wages, housing assistance, scholarships and reservations. He argued that voting rights should not be made a condition for receiving welfare benefits."Today, Panchayati Raj schemes. Tomorrow, rations? Pensions? MGNREGA? Housing? Scholarships? Reservations? This isn't politics to win elections—it's an arrangement to steal elections and a permanent setup to cling to power.Voting is your right, not a condition. A poor person's pension cannot be enslaved to their voter card. This isn't just vote theft—it's rights theft. We won't let this happen," he said.Singh, also known as Lallan Singh, had announced that beneficiaries seeking financial assistance and welfare payments under schemes of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj would need to provide an Elector's Photo Identity Card (EPIC) number and undergo mandatory biometric authentication. The proposed system would use voter ID instead of Aadhaar for identifying beneficiaries.The announcement has raised questions about the scope of the move, as the Ministry of Panchayati Raj does not directly operate schemes involving payments to individual beneficiaries. Aadhaar is currently used for beneficiary identification and payments under several other central government programmes, including rural housing assistance, PM-KISAN and social security pensions.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi accuses Centre of linking welfare benefits to voter lists amid SIR row. Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh announced that voter ID cards would be used instead of Aadhaar to identify beneficiaries of social welfare programmes under the ministry of panchayati raj. 18, the Jharkhand government issued a notification cancelling 22 recruitment examinations, including the 11th to 13th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) examinations, following public protests over alleged irregularities.Two days later, on August 20, the Jharkhand High Court stayed the state government's order cancelling the appointments of government employees recruited through the 11th to 13th JPSC examinations.The high court had earlier deferred hearings on petitions challenging the cancellation of JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations and appointments, scheduling the next hearing for September 18.The court fixed the date after the state government sought additional time to file its affidavit.The government had previously been directed to submit the affidavit by September 7 but failed to do so within the stipulated period.The cancellation of the JSSC CGL examination had triggered protests by candidates, including those who had already secured government appointments through the recruitment process.In a protest held after the cancellation announcement, appointed candidates questioned the government's decision and demanded an opportunity to present their side.One of the protesters, Chanda Kumari, told news agenct PTI that thousands of candidates who had secured appointments had been affected by the decision.She questioned whether cancelling the examination would ensure justice and action against those actually responsible for the alleged irregularities.“Our judiciary and democracy function on the principle that even if 100 guilty people go free, one innocent person should not be punished. But with the government's decision, thousands of innocent people have been punished immediately,” she said.Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who had been on a 16-day hunger strike, ended his protest after the government announced the cancellations. He described the decision as a “huge victory for Jharkhand” but said his campaign for recruitment reforms would continue, the earlier report said.Meanwhile, the Jharkhand Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has arrested two accused in separate cases linked to alleged irregularities in competitive examinations, officials said.In connection with alleged irregularities in the 14th JPSC preliminary examination, the CID arrested Sanjeet Kumar from the Ratu Road area of Ranchi.Kumar, who allegedly ran Shivangan Coaching Centre, is accused of acting as an agent and collecting money from candidates by promising to help them clear the examination, officials said.The alleged irregularities have also reached the Supreme Court. Last month, the apex court issued notices to the Centre, the Jharkhand government and others on a public interest litigation seeking a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) or an independent probe into alleged irregularities in the 2025 JPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana sought responses from the authorities on the petition filed by social worker Harisharan Devgan.Senior advocate Manan Kumar Mishra, appearing for the petitioner, told the bench that students had been continuously protesting over the alleged irregularities.The petitioner has sought directions for a fresh preliminary examination under safeguards approved by the Supreme Court.
Article Summary: Government sought more time to file affidavit in examination irregularities cases. CID arrests two accused in separate cases linked to alleged irregularities in competitive examinations. Jharkhand High Court quashes state government's decision to cancel the Jharkshand Staff Selection Commission Combined Graduate Level (JSSC CGL) examination.

Article Title: ‘Hope you are enjoying Delhi weather’: CJI blames vehicles as SC takes up air pollution case
Article Text:
Supreme Court flags traffic, stubble burning in Delhi-NCR

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday heard a suo motu case concerning air pollution in Delhi-NCR, with Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant expressing concern over rising pollution levels and stressing the need for measures to tackle vehicular emissions and stubble burning A bench comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana heard submissions from senior advocate Aparajita Singh, the amicus curiae in the matter, and the Centre's counsel.CJI Kant opened the hearing with the remark according to Live Law, "We hope all of you are enjoying Delhi weather." Singh responded that pollution levels were hovering around the severe category and said, "we are losing our voice as well. It's like smoking 30 cigarettes a day!"The CJI observed that pollution levels had fallen because it had rained in Delhi. Singh told the court that stubble burning contributed 14 per cent to pollution on November 5, but stressed that the national capital was already polluted before farm fires added to the problem."Transport is the biggest problem," she said, adding that authorities needed to focus on local sources of pollution as well as stubble burning. She pointed to transport, energy and waste burning as key concerns across the National Capital Region (NCR).On stubble management, the CJI said that the sowing season for farmers was under way and that stubble burning should have stopped. Singh, however, said farmers faced difficulties even when equipment was provided to them."To farmers, even if you give equipment, they don't have fuel. Price of fuel this year I don't have to highlight. Secondly, it does not work in small farms," she told the bench.Also read: Delhi air quality worsens, AQI hits 389 as several areas turn ‘severe’; GRAP-II measures underway Justice Bagchi referred to a proposal by authorities to acquire stubble at a fixed rate. The CJI suggested that the procurement rate should be announced in advance and that machinery should be provided to gram panchayats, as individual farmers could not afford the cost of such equipment."This machine needs to be given to Gram Panchayat. Individuals cannot afford. This is how machine can work. Cost of machine itself," the CJI said.The court also discussed the possibility of creating storage facilities for collected stubble. The CJI said that warehousing could provide an additional source of income for those involved in the process. The Additional Solicitor General (ASG) said a scheme was already in place and agreed to raise the suggestions with the Agriculture Ministry.The ASG told the bench that the government had taken several measures to address stubble burning and that farm fires had reduced significantly this year, particularly in Haryana. He also referred to financial incentives introduced by the state.Turning to vehicular pollution, the ASG said measures included phasing out diesel-operated rickshaws and mandating buses from other cities entering Delhi. The CJI, however, stressed that traffic congestion on roads connecting Delhi with the NCR remained a major concern."Major cause is vehicular pollution. Look at the roads in Delhi, connecting to NCR. The kind of bumper to bumper vehicles are going," the CJI said.He also flagged the lack of adequate public transport. The ASG said significant progress had been made in this area and that the authorities were considering immediate and intermediate measures.Singh pointed out that an earlier court order concerning toll plazas had not been fully implemented. She said vehicles were being stopped at NCR borders and made to idle, adding to pollution. The ASG conceded that implementation of the order was incomplete.The bench also discussed the impact of seasonal weather conditions on pollution levels. Singh said smoke disperses during summer but remains trapped during winter.The CJI called for greater awareness of traditional practices and questioned why people could not return to their original customs. Singh said that reverting to the use of diyas during Diwali would be ideal, while highlighting that poorer sections of society were among those most affected by pollution.The CJI observed that the Diwali period was also an important source of livelihood for poorer people, but said those who could afford to make firecrackers a social status symbol were contributing to the problem."Poor people do not generate any pollution. They are the sufferers. It is those who can afford it and those who can contribute to it,” the CJI remarked.The ASG said Delhi's geographical location made it difficult for smoke to disperse. The CJI then questioned whether scientific methods had been adopted to address the problem, observing that other measures had been "Tried and failed tools".The ASG said the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) regulated activities according to pollution levels, adding that Delhi attracted people from across the country and that every activity generated pollution. "We are only doing management," he said.The CJI pointed to the city's high pollution levels, remarking, "it's already touching 400!"Meanwhile, Delhi continued to reel under high pollution levels on Friday. The city's overall Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 389 in the 'very poor' category at 8 am, according to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).Several monitoring stations recorded AQI levels in the 'severe' category. IIT Delhi and Rohini reported an AQI of 474 each, followed by Punjabi Bagh at 465, RK Puram at 443, ITO at 422, Firoz Shah Road at 420 and India Gate at 403.Other areas also recorded high pollution levels, with Anand Vihar and Akshardham reporting an AQI of 359. IGI Airport Terminal 3 recorded 385, while the readings stood at 393 in Aya Nagar and 391 in Chandni Chowk.Municipal authorities deployed truck-mounted water sprinklers around India Gate as part of water-sprinkling operations under Stage II of the GRAP.According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Delhi recorded a minimum temperature of 17.8 degrees Celsius on Friday morning, with mainly clear skies. The weather department forecast shallow fog over the next four days, followed by fog or mist during the early morning hours of November 10 and 11.Residents continued to report discomfort amid the deteriorating air quality.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Friday heard a suo motu case concerning air pollution in Delhi-NCR. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant expressed concern over rising pollution levels. He stressed the need for measures to tackle vehicular emissions and stubble burning. The court discussed the possibility of creating storage facilities for collected stubble.

Article Title: 'Rahul's offer to debate still stands': Tharoor challenges BJP amid SIR, vote theft row

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Friday backed Rahul Gandhi 's offer to debate the government's allegations in Parliament, saying the House should reconvene as it has not yet been prorogued."Parliament has not yet been prorogued, so let it reconvene. If Parliament reconvenes, I believe Rahul Gandhi's offer to debate still stands," Tharoor said.Tharoor also criticised the Election Commissiono ver its handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging procedural irregularities and saying the Supreme Court hearings had supported the Opposition's concerns.Commenting on the ECI's decision to de-link the SIR declaration from Form 6, Tharoor described it as one of the Commission's "most outrageous mistakes". He alleged that the ECI, under Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, had made unauthorised changes to electoral procedures and permitted the bulk filing of Form 7 objections, resulting in people being denied their voting rights."The ordinary public has not fully understood all of these examples of frankly bureaucratic and administrative malfeasance that were conducted by the Election Commission under Gyanesh Kumar.Some of these things were objected to by the two other Election Commissioners as well. One of them is Form Six, where you suddenly unilaterally change the form, introducing a new declaration which is not authorized under the rules and laws of the country. ..This is what the opposition was complaining about...Under this election commission, bulk filling of Form 7s with thousands of names has been permitted, including in states like West Bengal. And as a result, on the basis of mere suspicion, a large number of people were denied the right to vote."Tharoor said the Opposition had sought not only Kumar's resignation but also a reversal of decisions taken during the SIR exercise that had allegedly affected eligible voters. He welcomed the ECI's move to roll back some of its decisions but said the consequences of earlier actions also needed to be reversed."But what has been done by the Election Commission now to roll back some of their mistakes, that is one of the things we asked for. We wanted not just Mr. Gyanesh Kumar's resignation; we wanted very much that the electoral process under the SIR should be reversed, that you should actually end up with these wrong decisions cancelled and their consequences for innocent Indian citizens be reversed...We've had an extraordinary number of 113 million votes cut from the register. For all of these reasons, what the Election Commission did was wrong; we have been saying it is wrong and the hearings in the Supreme Court are clearly demonstrating step by step that we were right and they were wrong," he said.Tharoor's remarks came amid a political confrontation between the Congress and the BJP over allegations of vote theft and the functioning of the Election Commission.On Thursday, Union Home Minister Amit Shah challenged Rahul Gandhi to debate the allegations in Parliament, urging him to present his arguments in the House rather than take the political battle to the streets. Addressing a rally in Karnal, Haryana, Shah said Gandhi would not be able to handle the government's response."If you (Rahul Gandhi) wish to engage in a responsible discussion—if your concerns hold truth, substance, and logic—then come and discuss them inside Parliament. Let’s face each other head-on! But you won’t be able to handle the answers; as always, you will just run away," Shah said.Shah's challenge followed Rahul's call for an open debate with Prime Minister Narendra Modi a day earlier. The Congress leader had claimed he could prove within five minutes that the prime minister was a "deshdrohi" (traitor).Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also urged Modi to answer questions surrounding alleged vote theft. Responding to Rahul's challenge, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said Parliament was already the appropriate forum for such a debate and reminded him of his responsibilities as the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor backs Rahul Gandhi's offer to debate the government's allegations in Parliament. Says the House should reconvene as it has not yet been prorogued. Criticises the Election Commissiono ver its handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Article Text:

Around a decade and a half before Los Angeles elected her as its first Indian-origin mayor, Kerala-born Tamil Nithya Raman sat with residents of a south Chennai suburb to map the notorious traffic snarls that would routinely disrupt their lives.On Thursday, WhatsApp groups in Nanganallur were buzzing with messages claiming the face riding the crest of the blue wave along Southern California's glitziest skyline as one of their own.Someone wrote in about being part of the group of 10-odd residents she interacted with regularly as an urban planner helping find solutions to the suburb's civic problems. Another spoke of how "curious and eager" she was to understand local issues and use her expertise to resolve them."What we didn't know was that she would go on to be a politician and get elected as mayor of LA," said K Sankaran, ex-president of Thillai Ganga Nagar Residents' Welfare Association.The distance between Los Angeles and the Tamil Nadu capital, separated by 7,800-odd nautical miles, wasn't the only one to be bridged by mutual celebration of a bright, young politician straddling different worlds.Around 830km from Nanganallur, at Kumarapuram in Thiruvananthapuram, a nondescript two-storey house in a narrow lane off the main road resonated with more personal insights into the Nithya story.It was here that the mayor-elect has stayed during multiple visits to meet her aunt Vanaja Sankar and other family members."She is a good girl who has always cared deeply for the family. She would make regular visits to her grandparents in West Fort till they were around. She never fails to visit me whenever she is in Thiruvananthapuram. I am her oldest surviving relative here," said Vanaja, showing family albums containing her now-famous niece's pictures.Nithya (45) moved to Louisiana with her parents as a six-year-old and became a US citizen by 22. Armed with an urban planning degree from Harvard University, she arrived in Chennai at 23 and founded Transparent Chennai, a civic initiative under Centre for Development Finance at Institute for Financial Management and Research. It used data and community participation to tackle urban governance.Nithya worked on urban planning in Chennai from 2004 to 2013, including working closely with local citizens' groups to document civic problems."The collaboration involved organising community forums, mapping traffic problems and collecting data on public transport, pedestrian safety and gaps in civic infrastructure," said V Rama Rao, an activist from Lakshmi Nagar in Nanganallur. "The data was meant to be presented to Chennai traffic police and municipal corporations to help develop actionable solutions."Nithya has acknowledged her Chennai stint in interviews to international publications, saying her organisation mapped and evaluated public toilets across the city to identify what needed to be fixed. She also spoke about studying working conditions of recycling workers and helping them get recognition from the state govt.In Thiruvananthapuram, where Nithya was born in 1981, aunt Vanaja said her niece loved visiting Kovalam for its beach and prayed at the Sree Padmanabhaswamy temple. "Nithya studied at a private school in Thrissur before moving to the US. She likes leading a simple life and has a lot of empathy for the poor. Perhaps it was this quality that led her to public life in the US."Before immigrating to the US, Nithya's father, R Venkataraman, worked at Keltron while her mother, Sudha, was emploted with Indian Overseas Bank.
Article Summary: Nithya Raman is the first Indian-origin mayor of a major U.S. city. The 45-year- old moved to Louisiana with her parents when she was six. Armed with an urban planning degree from Harvard University, she arrived in Chennai at 23. She founded Transparent Chennai, a civic initiative.

Article Title: Special summary roll revision in 6 states, UTs; draft on Nov 30
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Thursday announced the annual Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha and Sikkim.The poll roll revision exercise seeks to enrol eligible voters, particularly young and first-time electors, and facilitate advance applications from those who will become eligible on April 1, July 1 and Oct 1, 2027. Draft rolls will be out on Nov 30. The final publication of electoral rolls will take place on Jan 21.Deletion applications must undergo field verification in cases involving repeated or multiple entries. EROs must personally cross-check deletions exceeding 2% of electors at a polling station. Furnishing Aadhaar details in Forms 6 and 8 will remain voluntary. No application for enrolment can be rejected for failure to provide Aadhaar.
Article Summary: The poll roll revision exercise seeks to enrol eligible voters, particularly young and first-time electors. Draft rolls will be out on Nov 30. The final publication of electoral rolls will take place on Jan 21. Furnishing Aadhaar details in Forms 6 and 8 will remain voluntary.
